column1: # The DEVELOPMENT cluster's stopped consumer groups.
# `position` is passed to `kafka-consumer-groups.sh --reset-offsets` as it stands, so it is any of
# Every group here is created by writing its committed offsets directly, without running a
# consumer, so it exists but has no members: Kafka reports it as `Empty`. Groups that are alive
# are containers running consume.sh, and the Compose stack starts them; there are none on this
# cluster, because a laptop with one developer's service on it does not have a fleet of consumers.
# ONE group, a little behind. That is the whole point of this cluster: it is what a small,
# uncomplicated deployment looks like, and the contrast with the production cluster's eight groups
# The developer's service, stopped at offset 1 in each of the three partitions while the topic
# holds sixteen records. Small, genuine, uneven lag — the sort of number you get when you stop a
# service with your debugger and go to lunch.
